findings.description: Read-only SHA-256 comparison found seven files differing from the context lock, including both production scripts, their adapter mirrors, and tests/test_code_graph_raw_hashes.py. Current script hashes are 1293eeb3cae6dd264fa65410bf44ed1922383160d4f66651911019458d026b14 and bcfeb0a732c6d570d6082b4198c9cb491ca249b349d09c027fa92c4a38fe90a1; verification-receipt.json binds different hashes. The later regression receipt also covers older script bytes and omits the raw-hash test file. Recorded passing results therefore do not establish functional verification of the current unit.

findings.description: Current code disables Git fsmonitor and retains --no-filters hashing, with two additional fsmonitor execution regressions in the current test file. The supplied V-GR1 evidence records four tests against earlier bytes; the current test file contains six test methods and has a different hash. No inspected scoped receipt establishes execution of the additional security regressions against the current scripts. Static safeguards alone do not close this evidence gap.
findings.required_resolution: Supply hash-bound execution evidence covering the current clean-filter, cache-migration, and fsmonitor regressions, with Git available and no relevant skips.
